teaching.hint: What order of the values must every valid result preserve, and how can each subtree be kept balanced?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A BST traversal yields the values in sorted order; choosing a middle value for each recursive subtree gives comparable left and right sizes.
solution_outline.approach: Extract all values in sorted order from the input BST, then recursively form a new tree by selecting a middle value of each remaining interval as its root.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Every recursive interval contains exactly its subtree’s values; left values are smaller than the root, right values larger, and their sizes differ by at most one.
solution_outline.correctness: The extraction preserves all input values. Midpoint splits preserve BST order and, inductively, bound child-height difference by one at each node.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time and `O(n)` auxiliary space for the values; extraction may use `O(n)` stack on a skewed input.
solution_outline.pitfall: Balancing only the original root does not ensure every descendant subtree is balanced.

common_wrong_turns: Assume the input is already balanced
Choose a midpoint without first obtaining sorted values
source_fidelity_notes: Allows any valid shape and retains the every-node balance definition.
